recipes.name: Creamy Saffron Shrimp with Gnocchi and Caramelized Onion
ingredients_raw: 20 peeled and deveined large shrimp (21 to 30 per pound)

steps.text: Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Stir in onion, mushrooms, and brown sugar. Cook and stir until onion has cooked to a deep brown color, about 10 minutes. Remove caramelized onions to a plate and set aside.

Meanwhile, fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rolling boil over high heat. Once water is boiling, stir in gnocchi and return to a boil. Cook until gnocchi floats to the top, about 3 minutes; drain and keep warm.

Place the same skillet over medium-high heat and add shrimp. Cook and stir until shrimp have turned pink on the outside and are no longer translucent in the center, about 5 minutes. Add caramelized onions, sour cream, paprika, and saffron. Cook and stir until mixture begins to simmer, then gently fold in cooked gnocchi. Season with salt.
Pour gnocchi mixture into a serving dish and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese and basil to serve.

review.reviewBody: A good dish that could have been even better. I agree with Lynda Q that the amount of paprika was overkill. Less would be better and none better yet. Otherwise an interesting and tasty dish, largely because of the exotic flavor of saffron. Pairing the shrimp with the gnocchi was unexpected and delicious.

I made a few changes. I added sliced sweet peppers, just before caramelization was complete, making peppers soft, but not mushy. I also added about 2 tablespoons of minced garlic when adding shrimp. We like a little more kick, so I added black pepper at the end. Wow! This was really awesome and easy to make. I enjoy the way the original recipe is designed, as it is easy to make minor adjustments and change it up. Thank you for sharing

Really nice and easy recipe with a lot of flavor. As others, I left out the paprika and added more saffron to get the full flavor of this wonderful spice. I used yogurt in lieu of the sour cream I didn't have, straining it through a cheesecloth for 30 minutes to remove excess water. Also, after cooking the shrimp, which only takes a few minutes, I removed them from the liquid they had produced and reduced it before adding the rest of the ingredients. Will absolutely make again!

I have made this several times and have loved it every time! It is super simple, it's the timing that can be tricky. I put the water for the gnocchi on to boil first, then saute the onion and after a few minutes, add 1-2 zucchinis cut into cubes, then remove from the pan after less than 5 more minutes. Right as the water begins to boil for the gnocchi, I add the shrimp to the skillet, and then put the gnocchi in the pot to boil. After the shrimp is pink, I add the zucchini & onions (sometimes I don't use the mushrooms in the recipe) and the sour cream, plus cracked black pepper, and by then the gnocchi is ready to add. Once it's stirred together, I plate it, sprinkle it with the parmesan, and serve immediately. Soooo good - and I have to use dried basil, but it still tastes delicious! Thank you so much for a wonderful, easy, tasty recipe!

Mmm... It was sooo good! I was missing some ingredients, so I made a few substitutions. In place of sour cream, I used about 1/4-1/2 cup of heavy whipping cream. ( Guesstimation! I rarely measure when cooking this type of meal.) In place of butter, I used olive oil. I seasoned everything to taste, and for me that means I am heavy on the seasonings. In addition to the what was provided in the ingredient list, I added lots of garlic powder. Regarding the basil, instead of sprinkling the basil on top of the dish, I mixed it with the ingredients in step 3. Mushrooms were omitted because I did not have any on hand. Salt was omitted too.

Followed the recipe except used a little more saffron and smoked paprika. I sautéed the mushrooms, onion, brown sugar and added some fresh spinach. Then I added cooked, peeled deveined shrimp, I used 1.25lbs of small (approx 40-60 ct) and added the shrimp directly to the mixture. I stirred together smoked paprika, saffron, and sour cream, then added to shrimp mix. Stirred in gnocchi, topped with basil and cheese. Great flavor! Smoked paprika and saffron was fantastic.

Not crazy about these little potato things. They were terribly doughy. After cooking them, I fried them in olive oil. That helped a little. I added Italian chicken sausage. That helped too but I don't think I'll make it again.

Very Good the whole family of 8 loved it (except my 5 year old who wont eat anything) I doubled the recipe and used half Shrimp half Scallops...also made my own Gnocchi (not recomended unless you have lots of time and patience) and used more Saffron and less paprika as other posts have suggested... very good and will definately make again It was perfect for our Valentine's Day Family dinner.

I wish I could find saffron, store did not have it. Used an italian seasoning blend in its place. Decadent and easy. I would say to properly caramelize the onions you would need to cook for north of 10 minutes, we probably did 15+.

I'm giving this a 4-star rating; mainly because we didn't care for the brown sugar taste with the other flavors. Next time I'm simply going to sautee the onions and mushrooms in butter until soft, then add the other ingredients. The other ingredients created such a burst of flavors in the mouth! I had freshly grated parm/regianno cheese we used at the table and I added just a little extra basil. Wow!

I pair this with the sweet potato gnocchi recipes on here and I've made this a few times with some slight modifications with what is on hand. I used no-fat yogurt for the sour cream and since I had no saffron so I pumped up the paprika. Maybe my taste buds are weird compared to some of the other reviews but I found the increased pop from the spice very pleasant and the added smokiness a nice compliment to the sweet potato gnocchi.
I loved it with the gnocchi but my husband wasn't a fan. I think it would be great with pasta. So I will try that next.

Easy to make! Had to use cashew yogurt instead of sour cream so everyone could eat it. I can’t eat without garlic so I added garlic. I love gnocchi but not with tomato sauce so this was a great alternative to pesto.

Chose this recipe to pair with saffron noodles. The results were delicious. The shrimp were tender and paired well with the mushrooms and onions. I did up the volume of sour cream and milk to enjoy more sauce with the noodles.
It was great I did not use the over abundance of paprika but besides that it uses 2 of my favorite ingredients Shrimp & Gnocchi
I didn't make any changes since it was my first time. It was delicious! The one thing I will change the next time I make it will be a little more saffron and a little more sour cream.
I was wonderful very unusual flavor and easy to make.
Love this dish! Being Hungarian, the paprika was far from overwhelming. I make this every two weeks or so. So simple, yet lovely flavors.

I enjoyed the recipe but I guess I don’t know how to make gnocchi that well. I’ve only made it with soup one time and it was really smoochy. With all the veggies I put in it just had a different taste than expected. I followed the directions and wasn’t as expected, but everything else was delicious.
Made gnocchi from scratch. Easy to folly recipe. It was yummy!
